hypothesis: Train both the current-best single-task BPR-FM and iter 14's multi-task FM_MT (shared embeddings, auxiliary is_like head, alpha_aux=0.03 — its best swept value) independently, then average their standardized (z-scored) valid/test prediction scores into one ensemble ranking. Since the two models differ only in whether a second, less-noisy is_like gradient regularizes the shared embeddings, their errors are likely to be at least partially decorrelated, so averaging should reduce variance enough to cross the acceptance margin even though neither model alone did.
reflection: The pop-popularity-reweighting sweep collapsed exactly to alpha=0 (no improvement, and the curve shows the usual epoch-6 overfit peak), confirming the FM+BPR mechanism at k=16 is now fully saturated on every single-mechanism training-procedure/feature lever tried so far. Per the harness's own flag, two independent past candidates (iter 14's multi-task FM_MT and the plain BPR FM that's the current best) already individually land at or above 0.6035 without clearing the acceptance margin — averaging their predictions is the untried lever that doesn't require finding a new single mechanism, just combining two already-validated ones.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, because ensembling mainly smooths per-user pairwise ordering noise (what GAUC directly measures via averaged per-user AUC), whereas nDCG@5's top-5 cutoff is more sensitive to genuinely different top-ranked items and less helped by averaging two similar rankings.
